findings.analysis: The overview's metadata omission is addressed by registering one representative exception-log collection task for each of Armeria, Ratpack, Vert.x Web, and Wicket. All 18 signal-mode variants now label their effective exception signal, with Ratpack also retaining its controller-telemetry condition. Actual collection produced correctly labeled HTTP exception events under all four instrumentation scopes. Related Vert.x and Wicket metadata descriptions no longer falsely claim they emit no telemetry.

Added the four representative log-mode tasks to .github/scripts/instrumentations.sh and matching metadataConfig labels to every logs and logs/dup variant in the five affected build files. Ratpack labels include otel.instrumentation.common.controller-telemetry.enabled=true before the exception-signal condition. Five integration tests passed across the four collected profiles; inspection confirmed their exception events have the correct scope, severity, attributes, and when label. A Gradle task-graph check additionally verified effective properties and labels for all 18 variants without executing those additional variants.

[Testing] The new exception-log profiles for Armeria, Ratpack, Vert.x Web, and Wicket are not registered in `.github/scripts/instrumentations.sh`, so metadata regeneration omits their new logs. Register representative log-mode tasks for each integration and set matching `metadataConfig` system properties in their build files. Use `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs` (or `logs/dup` for that mode); for Ratpack, retain `otel.instrumentation.common.controller-telemetry.enabled=true` in the comma-separated label. Without these labels, collection classifies the logs as default telemetry, or as controller-only telemetry for Ratpack. Equivalent version suites need not all be collected. This follows `.github/instructions/instrumentation-gradle.instructions.md:59-75`; `instrumentation/hbase/hbase-client-2.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts:60-68` shows the existing labeling pattern.

Exception paths in Armeria, Ratpack, Vert.x Web, and Wicket now honor the configured exception signal while preserving span ownership, status, unwrapping, and trace correlation.

- **Configuration:** `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs` emits exception logs without span events; `logs/dup` emits both.
- **Coverage:** Verify exception event and log counts and correlation in default, `logs`, and `logs/dup` modes across supported versions.
